office.title: Indiana State Representative
office.summary: Members of the Indiana House of Representatives write and vote on state laws as part of the Indiana General Assembly. The House has 100 members, each representing one district for a two-year term [1].
duties: Introduces and votes on state legislation as one of the two chambers of the Indiana General Assembly [1].
Must be at least 21 years old when taking office and have lived in the district for at least a year [1].

incumbent.name: Bob Morris
incumbent.summary: Bob Morris, a Fort Wayne small-business owner, has represented House District 84 since 2010 and chairs the House Commerce, Small Business and Economic Development Committee [3]. In 2026 he filed a bill to require that execution teams be made up of volunteer legislators, saying he opposes the death penalty [4].
record: Committees: Commerce, Small Business and Economic Development (chair); Employment, Labor and Pensions; Utilities, Energy and Telecommunications, according to the House Republican caucus [3].

2026: Filed HB 1287, requiring the state prison warden to select an execution team only from General Assembly members who volunteer, with their names public [4]. Morris said, "Don't give anyone a job that you wouldn't want to do yourself" [4]. WANE reported he came out against the death penalty in 2024 and that his earlier repeal bill, HB 1030, received no committee hearing [5].
2026: Co-authored HEA 1424, described by the caucus as supporting farmers and small businesses [6].

Voted yes on SEA 1, the 2025 property-tax law (April 10, 2025) [7] and HB 1032, the congressional redistricting bill (Dec. 5, 2025) [8]. Was recorded as excused on the April 25, 2025 vote adopting the HEA 1001 budget conference report [9].

race_context: House District 84 is in Allen County and includes part of Fort Wayne and most of St. Joe Township, according to the House Republican caucus [3].
Morris was reelected unopposed in 2024 [10]. Both nominees were unopposed in the May 5, 2026 primaries [10].

Key differences: Morris's legislative focus includes commerce and small business, and he joined other northeast Indiana legislators in highlighting a state utility-affordability review [3, 11]; Meehan's campaign focuses on cost of living, housing, child care and corporate tax breaks [12].
No debate or forum for this race was found.

candidates.summary: Incumbent since 2010 and chair of the House Commerce, Small Business and Economic Development Committee [3].
background: Small-business owner who has founded several ventures in the district; B.S. from Indiana University [3].

Former state-sworn reserve officer with the New Haven Police Department (2005–2006); serves on the boards of Purdue University Extension Service and Northeast Indiana Crime Stoppers, according to the caucus [3].
Moved to Fort Wayne in 1976 and graduated from Bishop Dwenger High School [3].
path_to_ballot: Unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Republican primary [10].

items: Says of the death penalty: "I do not believe that another human being should be taking a human life" [4]. Told 21Alive that if the law stands, "the same people who voted for it should fully understand what it means" [13].
Said the March 2026 IURC energy-affordability investigation, which included Indiana Michigan Power, "adds another layer of accountability" to HEA 1002 [11].
On HEA 1424: "Farmers and small business owners work hard to provide quality products to their communities" [6].

on_incumbent: Is the current officeholder. No public statements about his challenger were found.
plans: No 2026 campaign platform was found; his campaign domain points to his caucus page [14].
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or fundraising figures were verified.
gaps: No campaign issue statements for 2026 were found.
Final status of HB 1287 was not confirmed; a search snippet suggested it did not advance.

candidates.summary: Misti Meehan is a small-business owner who says she has worked more than a decade with the Allen County Election Board [15]. She was unopposed in the Democratic primary [10].
background: Small-business owner; served in the Indiana Army National Guard [15].
Says she has worked with the Allen County Election Board for over a decade [15].
In 2019 she was chair of the Allen County Democratic Party and announced a run for the 1st District seat on the Fort Wayne City Council [16].
Attended Northrop High School and IPFW; says she was born and raised in the community [15].
path_to_ballot: Unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary [10].

items: Says "too many working people are struggling while large corporations receive tax breaks and special treatment" and that businesses must succeed "but not on the backs of Hoosier families" [12, 17].
Says "Families are being priced out of their own communities" [12].
Says "childcare has become unaffordable or unavailable for many" [12].

on_incumbent: No statements about Morris or his record were found on her website [17].
plans: Says she wants "practical solutions that lower costs, strengthen our local economy" [12] and to bring "practical, bipartisan leadership back to the Statehouse" [17].
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or fundraising figures were verified.
gaps: No news coverage of her 2026 campaign was found.
Her website offers no specific policy proposals.
Outcome of her 2019 city council bid not checked.
